summary: The Standard reports that German horse trainer Stephanie Kirchner, 33, swapped her SUV for a horse-drawn carriage to cut commuting costs after fuel prices rose following Russia's invasion of Ukraine. She says she saves around £212 per month, though her 3.5-mile commute now takes up to an hour instead of 10-15 minutes. The article also places her choice within Germany's sharp rise in energy prices and notes record UK pump prices for petrol.
one_line: German horse trainer Stephanie Kirchner replaced her SUV with a horse carriage for her commute to save money amid rising fuel prices.
key_facts: Stephanie Kirchner, 33, is a horse trainer and horse farmer from Schupbach near Limburg, Germany, who swapped her SUV for a horse-drawn carriage to save money on her commute.
Kirchner said she decided "it can't go on like this" after fuel prices jumped following the Russian invasion of Ukraine.
Kirchner said she suspected hay harvesting and everything else would become much, much more expensive, so "we have to save a little money".
Kirchner's three-and-a-half mile journey from Schupbach to work has grown from 10-15 minutes to as long as an hour.
Kirchner said she had saved around £212 per month by making the switch to the horse-drawn carriage.
Some people are annoyed if they can't get past me fast enough, Kirchner said, while the carriage is popular with local children.
Kirchner said: "I can't put a horse in a parking garage" and that more horse riders would do it if opportunities were created for the horses.
Germany is heavily reliant on Russian energy exports and has seen a sharp rise in gas and oil prices following Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine on February 24.
The Federal Statistical Office reported that energy prices as a whole were up 87.3 per cent compared to April 2021.
Power plants had to pay four times as much as a year before, and electricity prices rose by 87.7 per cent year on year.
Germany is Europe's biggest natural gas consumer and, apart from Russia, receives pipeline gas from Norway, the Netherlands, Britain and Denmark.
The average pump price for petrol in the UK reached 167.64p a litre, according to the RAC, above the previous record of 167.30p set on March 22.
The article was written by Daniel Keane and published on 20 May 2022.
